audience: National interoperability authority · ministry CIO · development-partner lead

videos.title: Why interoperability can't be bought, only built
videos.message: Procurement rules can require interoperability. Only whole-of-government planning delivers it — and once the framework exists, procurement is how you enforce it.

videos.title: The four layers of interoperability
videos.message: Interoperability fails at whichever of the four layers — Technical, Semantic, Organisational, Legal — you skip. The framework makes you address all four on purpose.

videos.title: The once-only promise
videos.message: Once-only — the state never asks a citizen for the same data twice — is the outcome interoperability is for, and the test of whether it works.

videos.title: The Strategic Foundation Document
videos.message: Name the mandate, the scope and the principles once, in writing, before any wiring — it is what every later decision is checked against.

videos.title: The Use-Case Catalogue
videos.message: Turn your integration map into a ranked catalogue of exchanges worth building — and start with the one that removes the most counters for citizens.

videos.title: Mapping your stakeholders
videos.message: Sort the agencies into Champions, Early Adopters and Observers, and you know who to onboard first and who to convince.

videos.title: What the world already proved
videos.message: Estonia's X-Road and the EU's once-only systems show the pattern; the education semantic standards show the vocabularies you will reuse rather than invent.
